questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p\in(0,1)$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C>0$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W>0$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. If both entry probabilities are halved, to $q_C/2$ and $q_W/2$, how does the belief $\mu=\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})$ change?
options: It halves, since the numerator $q_Cp$ halves
It moves towards the prior $p$, since entry becomes rarer
It moves towards $\frac{1}{2}$, since both types enter less often
It is unchanged, since only the ratio $q_C/q_W$ matters

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. In the belief $\mu=\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})=\dfrac{q_Cp}{q_Cp+q_W(1-p)}$, what does the denominator $q_Cp+q_W(1-p)$ represent?
options: The probability that the entrant is competitive
The total probability that entry is observed
The probability that a weak entrant enters
The probability that both types enter together

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Suppose both types enter with the same probability, $q_C=q_W>0$. What is the incumbent's belief $\mu=\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})$?
options: $\mu=\frac{1}{2}$, since both types behave the same way
$\mu=q_C$, the common entry probability
$\mu$ is unrestricted, as entry reveals nothing
$\mu=p$, as entry carries no information

questions.question: In Year-1 Bayes' rule the likelihoods $\mathbb{P}(\text{evidence}\mid\text{type})$ are given. When Bayes' rule is applied to beliefs in a game with an entrant of private type, where do the likelihoods $q_C,q_W$ of the observed action come from?
options: From Nature, which draws them together with the type
From each entrant type's equilibrium strategy
From the incumbent's own choice of beliefs
From the common prior over the entrant's types

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. In the profile under study neither type enters, so $q_C=q_W=0$. What does Bayes' rule imply for the belief $\mu$ the incumbent would hold after an entry?
options: Nothing: $\mu$ can be any number in $[0,1]$
It must equal the prior $p$
It must equal $0$, since no type enters
It must equal $\frac{1}{2}$, since nothing distinguishes the types

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Let $p=0.4$, $q_C=1$ and $q_W=\frac{1}{2}$. What is the incumbent's belief $\mu=\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})$?

A potential entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $0.3$ and weak ($W$) otherwise. The weak type always enters and the competitive type always stays out. After observing entry, what probability $\mu$ should the incumbent assign to $C$?

A job applicant is able with prior probability $\frac{1}{2}$. Able applicants apply with probability $0.8$ and less able ones with probability $0.2$; the employer sees only that an application arrived. What is its Bayes-consistent belief that the applicant is able?

Player 1 plays $T$, $M$, $B$ with probabilities $0.2$, $0.3$, $0.5$. Player 2 learns whether $B$ was played but cannot tell $T$ from $M$, so after $T$ or $M$ she is at a two-node information set. What belief must she place on the node after $T$?

An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Let $p=0.3$, $q_C=0.9$ and $q_W=0.2$. What is the probability $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(\text{entry})$ that the incumbent's information set after entry is reached?

An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. With $0<p<1$ and $q_C>0$ fixed, the weak type starts entering more often (larger $q_W$). How does the belief $\mu=\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})$ change?
options: It falls, since entry becomes more typical of type $W$
It rises, since entry is observed more often
It stays at the prior $p$, as the prior is unchanged
It is unaffected, since only $q_C$ appears in the numerator

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. With $0<p<1$, in which case does raising $q_W$ (keeping it positive) leave the belief $\mu=\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})$ unchanged?
options: When $q_C=1$, so that type $C$ always enters
When $p=\frac{1}{2}$, so that the types are equally likely
When $q_C=0$, so that $\mu=0$ for every $q_W>0$
When $q_W>q_C$, so that entry already points to $W$

questions.question: An incumbent is certain ex ante that an entrant is weak: the prior probability of a competitive type is $p=0$. A competitive type would enter with probability $\frac{1}{2}$, a weak one enters with probability $\frac{1}{3}$. After observing entry, which belief in the competitive type is consistent with Bayes' rule?
options: Unrestricted, since type $C$ never reaches the node
$\frac{1}{2}$, the competitive type's entry probability
$0$, since a type with prior $0$ keeps posterior $0$

questions.question: An entrant has one of three types, $A$, $B$, $C$, with prior probabilities $0.5$, $0.3$, $0.2$, and enters with probabilities $0.2$, $0.5$, $1$ respectively. The incumbent observes entry only. What is its belief that the entrant is of type $C$?

An entrant is competitive ($C$) with probability $0.2$, weak ($W$) otherwise; $C$ always enters, $W$ enters with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. After seeing entry the incumbent can fight (payoff $-3$ against $C$, $1$ against $W$) or accommodate (payoff $0$). Using its Bayes-consistent belief, what should it do?
options: Fight; fighting yields $0.2$
Accommodate; fighting yields $-\frac{1}{3}$
Accommodate; fighting yields $-1$
Accommodate; fighting yields $-\frac{5}{3}$

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Let $p=\frac{1}{4}$ and $q_C=\frac{1}{2}$. Which entry probability $q_W$ of the weak type makes the incumbent's belief after entry equal to $\mu=\frac{1}{3}$?

An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Assume $0<p<1$ and entry has positive probability. Which condition is necessary and sufficient for observing entry to raise the belief in $C$ above the prior, $\mu>p$?
options: $q_Cp>q_W(1-p)$
$q_C>q_W$

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Let $p=0.3$ and suppose each type enters only by mistake, with $q_C=q_W=0.001$. What restriction does Bayes' rule place on the belief after entry?
options: None, since entry is practically never observed
$\mu=0.001$, the entry probability of each type
$\mu=0.3$, since entry has positive probability
$\mu=\frac{1}{2}$, as both types enter equally rarely

questions.question: An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Let $p=0.4$. Under some entry probabilities, entry occurs with probability $0.6$ and leads to belief $\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})=0.5$. What is the belief $\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{no entry})$?

An entrant is competitive ($C$) with prior probability $p$ and weak ($W$) otherwise; type $C$ enters with probability $q_C$ and type $W$ with probability $q_W$. The incumbent sees entry but not the type. Let $p=0.4$, $q_C=0.9$, $q_W=0.3$; then $\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{entry})=\frac{2}{3}$. What belief $\mathbb{P}(C\mid\text{no entry})$ should the incumbent hold if the entrant stays out?
